messages:
nina: quick flag: we've got drift between ingest events and ledger for long chat sessions. tokenizer sometimes mutates attribution keys (appends `#vX`) and ledger joins fail.
sam: can you paste a tiny trace so i can repro locally?
nina: sure (sanitized):
```
ingest: {session: s-77, fingerprint: f-77, attribution: tenant:42}
tokenizer: {session: s-77, fingerprint: f-77, attribution: tenant:42#v2}
billing: {session: s-77, fingerprint: f-77, attribution: tenant:42}
```
match failed because tokenizer added version suffix.
jordan: so non-canonical keys across services. is this only for async tokenization?
nina: mostly yes. tokenizer adds heuristics `#v*` to reduce collisions when running parallel tokenizers. ingest doesn't strip it.
tara: do we have a stable provenance_id in the envelope we can use instead?
evan: provenance_id exists for chunked requests but is optional for older clients. not reliable everywhere.
sam: options i see: (a) canonicalize in ingest (strip suffix) -> adds CPU on hot path; (b) tokenizer emits a canonical_attribution field and a mapping sidecar event -> keeps ingest cheap; (c) rely on fingerprint+session join -> brittle. thoughts?
jordan: (a) risks adding latency to ingest and broad deploy surface. (b) seems cleaner but trust boundary shifts to tokenizer. (c) is last-resort.
ops-bot: note: ingest hot-path changes require a canary plan across ~12 services. :warning:
tara: for audits we should emit an immutable mapping event anyway: `mapping: {original -> canonical}` so replays/audits can reconcile.
nina: proposal: tokenizer writes `canonical_attribution` and emits a sidecar mapping event (fanout to audit-topic). ingest will accept `canonical_attribution` if present and persist it; otherwise route to best-effort postprocess queue and flag for manual replay.
evan: tradeoffs: extra storage + fanout cost vs keeping ingest CPU low. i'm +1 for sidecar mapping prototype.
sam: i'll spike the mapping-event shape and measure throughput impact. can do a small harness.
jordan: i'll implement the postprocess consumer that reconciles late mapping events with ledger entries and expose metrics.
tara: i'll draft an audit playbook describing replay steps and how to run reconciles if mapping events are missing/late.
nina: can we get a spike + playbook by EOW? sam you ok to own the spike?
sam: yep. will post PR with perf numbers and canary plan. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: reminder: include rollout/canary steps if any ingest behavior changes.
note: no title per slack doc rules
